- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with downward momentum.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast 3–5 days post-spike.
- Forecast mean reverts to 10–15 day average; if model is 3–5% above that, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses early trend reversals; if sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 5 days, reduce forecast 1–2% per day for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “low-high-low” patterns, model tends to overreact to lows; apply a “floor correction” — cap forecast at 10% below recent 7-day low if sentiment is weak.
